scope: P32 first selected unloaded-history text-search slice; generic capability-driven interface with one reviewed official app-server route

behavior.selection: User explicitly selects at most 20 existing Farfold index rows from one Agent. Backend captures exact AgentRow and complete SessionRow metadata; front end supplies no native id, cwd, launch command or config.
behavior.ownership: Reject selected native history loaded under any owned directory/service of the same Agent, or a proven LaunchIdentity alias. Existing AccountScope also rejects busy/unsettled/candidate work and blocks new affected work until real cleanup. This is not account-wide or all-external-process discovery.
behavior.worker: Existing global execution 2-slot lease, ActivityPermit, configuration guard and AccountScope are held by actual blocking worker. Real owned child/group/pipes settle before terminal release; observers do not own worker lifetime.
behavior.publication: Page counts remain progress only. Current-row hit text and final row status remain private until actual child cleanup, original directory-handle identity and exact source metadata recheck. Publish serializes with cancellation. Earlier verified rows remain available. Invalid/repeated-cursor pages never contribute hits; valid earlier pages can remain partial if source still verifies.
behavior.pendingCleanup: Once a previous child really exits, the next row returns to running/code:null; cancellation prevents continuing. No claim that sending cancellation is already stopped.
behavior.body: Only individual official user text parts and assistant text blocks. Tools, reasoning, attachments and other message kinds explicitly excluded. Original native turn/item ids and partIndex identify each bounded result. No fabricated live ThreadState or automatic open/restore.
behavior.matching: Unicode per-scalar lowercase literal substring. UTF16 ranges address returned original plain-text window; separate user parts never concatenate. Exact query bytes retained; no regex/semantic/OCR claims.
behavior.storage: RAM only; no persistent transcript, event ledger or body index. Settled detail can be released or pruned after 300s access; used-id compact tombstones survive process lifetime. No private Agent history/config files read.
